speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent; can you tell me exactly when you first noticed the weakness and decreased sensation in your right arm? Did it happen suddenly or did it develop gradually over time?

speaker: Patient
text: 55-year-old male bodybuilder. The patient has been experiencing weakness in his right arm for a few weeks, which has progressively worsened to the point of dropping objects. He also reports a recent unexplained weight loss of 17 pounds and has a history of diabetes. The patient admits to chronic alcohol use, heavy smoking, and anabolic steroid use.

speaker: Doctor
text: Have you experienced any numbness or weakness in your legs or face, and do you have any difficulty swallowing or speaking? Also, have you noticed any changes in your bowel or bladder function?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Weakness in the right arm. I also have Decreased sensation in the right arm, Dull aching and burning pain in the right arm, Significant weight loss.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your significant weight loss, history of steroid use, and the localized nature of your symptoms, I need to rule out a mass compressing your nerves. Do you have any history of recent trauma to your right shoulder or neck, and have you noticed any swelling or lumps in that area?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Diabetes Social history: Drinks 2-7 alcoholic beverages per day. Has smoked 2 packs of cigarettes per day since he was 25. Uses anabolic steroids.

speaker: Doctor
text: Doctor: Given your heavy smoking and unexplained weight loss, do you experience any persistent cough, chest pain, or shortness of breath? I also need to know if the pain in your arm radiates down to your hand or if you notice any muscle wasting in your right shoulder.

speaker: Patient
text: Denies recent fevers, changes in vision, difficulty speaking, or changes in balance.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your heavy smoking history and significant weight loss, I need to check for a lung tumor that may be compressing your nerves. REQUEST TEST: Chest CT with contrast and MRI of the brachial plexus.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: CT Chest: Solid mass at the apex of the right lung, suggestive of a tumor. Note: MRI of the brachial plexus was not included in the available test data.

speaker: Doctor
text: The chest CT confirms a solid mass at the apex of your right lung, which is highly suggestive of a Pancoast tumor compressing your brachial plexus. Given your smoking history and symptoms, this explains the arm weakness, pain, and weight loss. DIAGNOSIS READY: Pancoast tumor (superior sulcus tumor) causing brachial plexopathy.
